messages:
tyler (Procure): Looping folks — MeterForge sent the renewal quote. There's a big delta between committed vs metered. Quick Q: can committed credits be applied to deduped ingestion/embedding tokens (so we only pay on net tokens)? Quote attached (pdf).

maria (Finance): Can you paste the numbers here? need to model both paths. what's our current monthly token volume to baseline against?

tyler (Procure): Last month we saw ~1.2B tokens total (ingest + query). Pilot projection is ~2.5B/mo. MeterForge's sales sheet shows: commit $35k/mo = ~50% discount vs sticker; metered = $0.020 per 1k tokens. They also call out "context tokens" billed separately.

sam (EngInfra): We do client-side dedupe before sending, but MeterForge claims they also run a server-side dedupe pipeline. Important: do they dedupe across time windows? across customers? and do they exclude context tokens?

maria (Finance): If commit credits can't apply after dedupe, the savings evaporate. Tyler — ask them if commit applies to net tokens after dedupe and whether embedding reuse/caching reduces billed volume.

tyler (Procure): Pinged sales: "Do committed credits apply post-dedupe? Do context tokens count toward the commit? Any seat fees or minimums we should know about?"

billing-bot: BillingOps note: previous MeterForge invoice INV-2026-03 flagged — 12% discrepancy vs our usage report. Ticket #1429 opened for recon.

elena (Legal): Also need to confirm true-up / termination language in SOW. If we commit and later drop usage, do they true-up back to us, or invoice us for shortfall? We should require a 30d notice or quarterly true-up with credits.

maria (Finance): Model impact: if commit applies post-dedupe and only counts unique tokens, commit plan likely wins. If they count before dedupe or include every context token, metered + negotiated volume discount + hard caps may be safer.

tyler (Procure): Vendor replied (copied from sales email): "Committed credits apply to net tokens after our deduplication pipeline; context tokens do count toward the commit; true-ups are quarterly with 30-day notice." They asked for our expected traffic to set tiering.

sam (EngInfra): Sounds promising but we need the technical definition of their "deduplication pipeline" — TTL/window, per-customer vs global dedupe, how they treat minor diffs, and whether we can audit a sample of the dedupe output. Also want SLA on dedupe processing and any edgecases where tokens are still billed.

maria (Finance): Numbers for modelling: baseline 1.2B tokens/mo, pilot peak 2.5B. Assume 20% dedupe net = ~1.6B. Tyler — with their numbers, what does the per-1k-net-token cost look like under commit vs metered?

tyler (Procure): Vendor sent a quick calc: "Commit $35k/mo covers up to 1.8B net tokens; overage billed at $0.015/1k. Metered listed at $0.02/1k." I'm drafting a short cost sheet now.

elena (Legal): Before we agree, add contract language: "committed credits apply only to tokens demonstrably deduplicated by vendor's production pipeline" and include right to audit a redacted sample of dedupe logs quarterly. Also define 'context tokens' precisely.

maria (Finance): Agreed. Can someone run a quick pro-forma comparing three options: (A) metered baseline at $0.02/1k, (B) commit $35k/mo with overage $0.015/1k, (C) commit $20k/mo with tighter overage cap. I'll own the spreadsheet if Tyler posts vendor breakouts.

tyler (Procure): Posted calc link (internal): https://redwood.internal/sheets/meterforge-renewal — also requested a sample dedupe report and the exact text definition of "context tokens" from sales.

sam (EngInfra): I'll run a mock dedupe pass on last 30 days of telemetry and post delta numbers by EOD so Finance has concrete net-token estimates.

tyler (Procure): 👍 thanks. TL;DR: if vendor confirms auditability + quarterly true-up + commits apply post-dedupe, Finance + Legal + Eng lean toward commit. If any of those fail, default to metered with negotiated caps and a hard overage ceiling.
